newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK pro-China politican calls Helms idea barbaric.
newsitem.headline: HK pro-China politican calls Helms idea barbaric.

text.p: A Hong Kong politican on Tuesday described as barbaric a proposal by a right-wing U.S. Senator to bar members of Hong Kong's provisional legislature from entering the United States.

The pro-Beijing politician, Liberal Party chairman Allen Lee, told reporters that Jesse Helms, chairman of the U.S. Senate's foreign relations committee, was biased and wrong and that he had sent the senator a letter urging him to think again.

"It is a barbarian act...legislature members cannot enter the United States," Lee said after emerging from a meeting with Hong Kong's post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa, who is preparing to take over from British Governor Chris Patten on July 1.

An aide to Helms, a fervent anti-Communist, said on Monday the North Carolina Republican was considering introducing a bill to ban Hong Kong's provisional legislators from visiting the U.S. after the colony returns to China in July, following more than 150 years of British rule.
Tung, chosen by China last month as post-colonial leader, said many U.S. Congressmen did not understand Hong Kong and he hoped they would devote more time to it, Hong Kong radio said.

The provisional legislature held its first meeting on Saturday over the border in China amid threats by the Democratic Party, the territory's largest, that it would go to court to get the body banned on grounds that it was unconstitutional.
Under Hong Kong's constitutional set-up it is illegal to have two legislatures operating at once, lawyers said.

China, angered by the expansion of democracy in the territory in the twilight of British rule, has vowed to disband the current elected legislature and install the provisional body at the stroke of midnight on June 30.
Britain has branded the move as unnecessary and challenged China to prove it conforms with a 1984 United Nations-registered treaty setting out the terms of Hong Kong's return to Beijing.
The provisional legislature was picked in December by the China-controlled Selection Committee.
China is also under fire from Britain and Washington over its plan to repeal laws on civil liberties after the handover.
Pro-democracy groups in Hong Kong say China's ultimate aim is to snuff out democracy in the territory.
